audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim on p.192-193 of the held archive.org PDF (page scan 2-3), scanned artefacts aside. (2) The deciding source is a 1978 SIL phonemic statement, the sole phonological description of this languoid; nothing better exists per Glottolog (Glottolog's fullest description is a phonology or text collection) and the SIL archive; the complete scan downloaded now adds the title page and the contrast-pair pages, which mark stress phonemically on penult or final syllables and contain no rule conditioning its position, consistent with the 'lexical' (penult~final, unpredictable) coding and the word domain. (3) No list of works to obtain: the remaining Glottolog items are syntax/discourse papers we already hold or a clitic-order thesis; Dawson 1958 and Collins 1970 describe Kalagan/Tagakaulo, not Kaagan. tone.quote: A phonological word is a sequence of syllables marked by the occurrence of primary stress. One syllable particles do not carry primary stress. Phonological words of from one to six syllables have been observed. [...] There are two degrees of stress, primary (') and secondary ("). A polysyllabic word has one primary stress and if there are three syllables preceding the primary stressed one, also a secondary stress. [...] Length does not survive without stress and is considered non-phonemic.

tone.quote: In addition, Wendel and Wendel (1978) conducted an extensive study of the phonemic statements of Kaagan-Kalagan, shedding light on its sound system and enhancing our understanding of Kalagan’s phonology. Their study stemmed from the speech of approximately 400 Kalagan-Kaagan individuals residing in Hagunoy. [...] The paper explores the phonemes within syllables, phonological words, length and stress, interpretation of /i/ and /u/, contrasts and description of phonemes, distribution of vowels, as well as consonant clusters across syllable boundaries.
